intro: A Southern gothic blues songwriter with a literary streak.
story: Adia Victoria, raised in Spartanburg, South Carolina and now based in Nashville, arrived at Pickathon in 2016 with her debut, Beyond the Bloodhounds, its title taken from Harriet Jacobs's 1861 narrative. Her fiercely literary take on Southern gothic blues carried on with Silences on Atlantic in 2019, then A Southern Gothic in 2021, made with T Bone Burnett, which the Americana Music Association nominated for Album of the Year. In September 2025 she played the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville.
artist_reel_line: In September 2025 she played the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville.

intro: A Canadian indie-rock band, newly reunited.
story: Wolf Parade, formed in Montreal in 2003 by Spencer Krug and Dan Boeckner, were newly reunited when they played Pickathon in 2016, a decade after Apologies to the Queen Mary on Sub Pop won them a place on the Polaris Prize shortlist. EP 4, their first new music since 2010's Expo 86, came out that May. Cry Cry Cry followed in 2017 and Thin Mind in 2020. In 2026 they shared a Trixie Mattel remix of I'll Believe in Anything and toured North America.
artist_reel_line: In 2026 they toured North America and shared a Trixie Mattel remix.

story: Protomartyr are a Detroit quartet, with Joe Casey's dry, literary baritone over jagged guitars, who were an ascending force when they played Pickathon in 2016, a year after The Agent Intellect on Hardly Art. Relatives in Descent, recorded at 64 Sound in Los Angeles with Sonny DiPerri, came on Domino in 2017 and Formal Growth in the Desert in 2023. Hotel Usona followed in 2026, with a North American and European tour.
artist_reel_line: Hotel Usona, on Domino, came out in 2026, with a tour of North America and Europe.
